title: Typed Command Descriptor

oracle.positive: Descriptor declares typed inputs/options/output and is serializable/deterministic
oracle.negative: Missing mandatory input or unregistered option rejected

reviewer.role: plan gate: this item requires no manual test
reviewer.statement: The plan records manual_test_gate=AUTO_ONLY for every L3 of OM9-L2-01-02, so acceptance rests on the automated checks below; no human item is requested.
reviewer.scope: no on-screen behaviour of its own: the descriptor and the availability rules are pure data

checks_run: RED: cargo test -p om9-core --test command_descriptor -> 4 passed; 2 failed. The product defect the fixture caught: the descriptor accepted an option whose name is only whitespace (E4), a name the parser can never match. The declared prompt/output/requires_input/preconditions were added in this round, so their absence was recorded in the crosswalk rather than as a failing assertion.
GREEN: cargo test -p om9-core --test command_descriptor -> 6 passed; 0 failed (5 positive cases, 4 negative cases)

code_change: capability.rs: Operation gains prompt, requires_input, output and preconditions (all serde-defaulted, so an older document still loads) and derives PartialEq.
capability.rs: Operation::option(name) returns the declared spelling without case, or UnknownOption naming the option and the command.
capability.rs: the option rule now trims and compares without case, so '  ' and 'Length'/'length' are refused instead of silently unusable.
